subject: Model omega-tau gradual tail inflation — temporary SLA carve-in / rollback decision
body:
From: Carl Jensen <carl.jensen@novatech.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: ops@novatech.com
Date: Sat, 24 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Notice: rising tail latency (p99) on Model omega-tau v3.2

Kimberly,

We started seeing a steady rise in p99 response time for the model labeled omega-tau v3.2 against our production traffic this morning. The increase is gradual but persistent — ~35% rise over baseline across the last 12 hours on our peak routes. No functional errors, just latency inflation causing user-facing timeouts on our side (timeouts set at 3.5s).

Attached is our export (p99_trend_export.csv) and a short screenshot of the dashboard. Can you advise whether there is a safe rollback path to the previous model (v3.1) and what the expected impact is on routing and quota? We need a decision window of ~2 hours if possible.

-Carl
Carl Jensen
Head of Platform Ops, Novatech

---

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Carl Jensen <carl.jensen@novatech.com>, ops@novatech.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 24 Jul 2027 09:34:18 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice: rising tail latency (p99) on Model omega-tau v3.2

Hi Carl — thanks for the heads-up and the data. We're pulling traces and looking at routing/queueing now.

Immediate answers:
- We can revert traffic to v3.1 within ~6 minutes for that customer route via the traffic pin override; no infra changes required.
- There is a small risk (rare) of token-level variance on completions for edge prompts; we will run a brief canary to validate behavior.

Looping in Ben (sales) and Neha (SRE) to coordinate the rollback vs. patched rollforward. Ben — can you confirm if Novatech is amenable to a brief canary rollback? Neha — can you prioritize an evidence pack (kernel/cold-start vs. runtime) and check if quantization profile changed for v3.2 deployments overnight?

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

---

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, Carl Jensen <carl.jensen@novatech.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 24 Jul 2027 11:03:02 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice: rising tail latency (p99) on Model omega-tau v3.2

Carl — quick follow from commercial side: Novatech is in month-to-month with committed throughput. If we roll back we'll do so with a short postmortem and offer a one-week credit if SLA breach confirmed. If they're open to a rollforward to a patched variant (v3.2.1) that addresses the KV-cache misalignment we've seen elsewhere, we could avoid traffic churn.

Are you open to a controlled rollforward canary (5% traffic) + immediate fallback plan? Marcus (runtime) — is the patch ready to roll?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

---

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, Carl Jensen <carl.jensen@novatech.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 24 Jul 2027 13:18:44 -0700
Subject: Re: Notice: rising tail latency (p99) on Model omega-tau v3.2

Quick findings from SRE (summary):
- The p99 rise correlates with a change in sequence-length distribution (Novatech pushed a content-policy batch at 03:00 UTC); that shifted average run-length for certain endpoints and exposed a kernel scheduling contention on some GPU types.
- No memory leaks or GC anomalies.
- Marcus: the patch for tighter KV cache evictions is packaged (proposed_patch_release_notes.md attached). We validated on staging with representative traffic; p99 improved ~22% vs v3.2 in our tests.

Given the data, my recommendation: do a rollforward canary to v3.2.1 on a small subset of Novatech routes (5% traffic) for 30 minutes. If metrics behave, promote; if p99 doesn't fall back within the window, perform immediate rollback to v3.1. We should also snapshot the node (cluster_metrics_snapshot.png) before any change.

I will own the rollout steps and the rollback playbook.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

---

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: Carl Jensen <carl.jensen@novatech.com>, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2027 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Decision and ask: temporary SLA carve-in and approval for rollforward canary

Team / Carl — after engineering validation, proposed operational plan is below. This is the decision I'm sending to leadership and Novatech. Please reply-all with approvals or veto within 1 hour.

Plan (rollforward canary):
- Target: Novatech prod route "/nlp/summarize" only, 5% of traffic at T+0.
- Duration: 30 minutes measured window.
- Success metric: p99 reduction >= 15% vs v3.2 baseline and no error-rate increase.
- Rollback: immediate automated pin to v3.1 if p99 > baseline for two consecutive 5-minute buckets.
- Customer impact mitigation: extend Novatech SLA tolerance by 48 hours (commercial credit if confirmed breach), and enable soft-timeout at 4.5s client-side guard.
- Evidence capture: attach p99_trend_export.csv, cluster_metrics_snapshot.png; will upload a full trace bundle to the Drive link.

Approvals needed:
- Ben (commercial): confirm acceptance of credit and outbound comms language.
- Marcus (runtime): confirm patch artifacts and deploy window (canary today between 16:00–18:00 PT).
- Jordan (product): sign off on functional equivalence risk.

Carl: if you prefer a direct rollback to v3.1 instead of the canary, please say so — we will prioritize rollback but note it may cause brief request retries during the transition.

Thanks,
Kim

From: Carl Jensen <carl.jensen@novatech.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2027 16:02:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Decision and ask: temporary SLA carve-in and approval for rollforward canary

Thanks Kim — Novatech accepts the canary approach. We prefer rollforward first; we'll escalate to rollback only if there is no steady improvement in the 30-minute window. Please proceed and confirm the canary start time. Also confirm the credit language and timeline for the postmortem.

-Carl
